title: Anglo Asia Education Foundation hosts student group from Mongolia
summary: A group of 13 students and parents from Mongolia arrived in the UK for a study tour organised by the Anglo Asia Education Foundation...
body:
Mongolian student group visit Frances Bardsley Academy for Girls

On Wednesday, 21st August 2019 a group of 13 students and parents from Mongolia visited Frances Bardsley Academy for Girls in North London as part of their UK study tour organised by the Anglo Asia Education Foundation.

Located in North London, Frances Bardsley is an excellent school and has provided an exemplary education for girls aged eleven to eighteen for over one hundred years. It is one of the few members of the Global Girls’ School Alliance.

Head teacher David Kindly presented participation awards to the students on the tour. The school introduced the school’s long history gave a lecture on English history.

Then in true British style, the students on the tour enjoyed English afternoon tea with some local students and teachers.

The visit helped students from the two countries form friendships which supports their learning about different cultures and languages.










Anglo Asia Education Foundation hosts masters classes for visiting students

On 17th August 2019 , Anglo Asia Education Foundation ran a number of Masters’ classes in Music and Drama in the Sir Alexander Fleming Building at Imperial College for a group of Mongolian students on their UK study tour.

The students attended three sessions of the masters’ classes. The first being a music master class by He Wu, a young up and coming Chinese born Soprano who has received support from AAEF in the UK. She studied at the Royal College of Music . She held her débute in Madame Butterfly at Iford 2018 finale as Madame Butterfly. The second Master’s class was in drama by Eton College drama student Andrew Aarons who has won a number of performance related competitions at Eton. The third class was an etiquette lesson held by Victoria Aarons who demonstrated to the students a number of key etiquette skills which included setting a table for dinner culturally very different to Mongolia.

The students enjoyed the classes which were unique to them. We hope that this will support them in learning western cultures and the English language going forward.
